compression.title: How does a video get small?
compression.lead: A video is a flipbook of many pictures. Without tricks, the file would be huge. Here are the tricks.
compression.merke: A video gets small because its pictures look alike. Only what is new gets saved, and details that the eye hardly sees may go.

basics.heading: 1. Picture, frame rate and resolution
basics.text: A frame is a single picture. A video shows many of them one after another, so fast that we see movement. Three numbers decide the size:

fps.text: How many pictures per second. 30 fps means 30 pictures in every second.

resolution.text: How many pixels a picture has. 1920 × 1080 pixels is called Full HD.

bitrate.text: How much data per second is stored in the file. The higher, the more detail and the bigger the file.

raw.heading: 2. Why raw video is huge
raw.text: Every pixel has red, green and blue, and each of these colours needs one byte. Then you calculate: width × height × 3 × pictures per second × seconds. Try it.
raw.afterText: A compressed video needs only a small part of that. In the example above it is about 10 megabit per second.

calc.resultLabel: Without compression the file would be:
calc.factor: Compressed, it is about {factor} times smaller.

flip.heading: 3. Trick 1: save only what is new
flip.text: The first picture is a keyframe. It is a complete picture. The following pictures are change pictures: they only save what changed since the picture before.
flip.text2: Press play or drag the slider. The turtle swims, the background stays the same. That is why most pictures have almost nothing to save.
flip.note: Real videos are even cleverer and often only remember where a part has moved. Here we simply count the changed pixels.
flip.liveLabel: Picture {n} from the film. Changed pixels are marked purple.
flip.liveCaption: The picture as you see it. Purple: it has changed.
flip.storedKeyCaption: The whole picture is stored, because it is a keyframe.
flip.storedChangeCaption: Only the changed pixels are stored. The rest stays empty.
flip.total: In total: {percent} % of the file compared to {frames} full pictures. {keyframes} of them are keyframes.

seek.heading: 4. Jumping into the middle of a video
seek.text: If you want to start at second 30, you cannot simply jump there. A change picture needs the picture before it. So the app starts at the last keyframe and rebuilds all pictures up to the target.
seek.resultDirect: Second {target} is a keyframe itself. The app jumps straight there.
seek.resultPlan: The app starts at second {keyframe}, the last keyframe before it. Then it rebuilds {frames} pictures up to second {target}.

lossy.heading: 5. Trick 2: leave out details
lossy.text: Some details the eye hardly sees. Lossy compression throws them away. That saves a lot of space. If you throw away too much, small blocks become visible.
lossy.note: The blocks are called blocks. JPEG compression works with blocks of 8 × 8 pixels. Turn on the blocks to see them.

jpeg.size: This section of the picture: {value} kB
jpeg.raw: Without compression the whole picture would be {value} MB
jpeg.originalLabel: Section of the original picture, enlarged
jpeg.compressedLabel: Section after compression at quality {quality} percent, enlarged
